  COVID-19 PUBLIC PARTICIPATION OPTIONS

Due to the existing COVID-19 health emergency and the social

address the Special Planning Commission Meeting of June 17, 2020
at 7:00 P.M. by telephone, video and other electronic means, as
follows:

Viewing and Listening to the Meeting without Making Public
Comments:
   On Spectrum Cable Local Channel 35 with audio and limited
  video. Please check with your cable provider for details.
   Live on-line through Facebook Live, with audio and limited
  video, at https://www.facebook.com/cityofinglewood/

Members of the public may listen and make oral public comments
telephonically by dialing:

  Dial-in: 1-888-251-2949 or 215-861-0694
  Access Code: 8284598##

Please observe the following tips when phoning in:

  instructions on how you can make public comments via phone.
    If you are calling from a cell phone, please call from an
  area with good reception.

  from the phone transmission.  Additionally, when you are
  making public comments on the phone line you will be inaudible

Written Public Comments: Members of the public can submit comments
for consideration by the Planning Commission by sending them to
Mindy  Wilcox,  AICP,  Planning  Manager  at
mwilcox@cityofinglewood.org. To ensure distribution to the members

comments must be received prior to 12:00 P.M. on January 20, 2021,
the day of the meeting. Correspondence should indicate the meeting
date and agenda item. Comments received after 12:00 P.M. and prior
to close of the public hearing will be made part of the official
public record of the meeting.

RECOMMENDATION
Consider the staff report and the public testimony and make a determination. If the

REQUEST
Design Review to allow exterior improvements to the storefront of an existing commercial
building on an approximately 18,000 square-foot property at 330 East Kelso Street.
 Design Review No. 2020-005 (DR-2020-005)  January 20, 2021
330 E. Kelso Street

BACKGROUND
Chapter 12, Article 10.2 and 14 of the Inglewood Municipal Code (IMC) states that in the
MU-1 zone, all exterior improvements (e.g., façade renovation, extension of parapets,
articulation of building walls and entrances, new doors and windows, etc.), extension of
building footprints, and new construction of buildings shall require Design Review
approval.

Design Review is governed by the following Inglewood Municipal Code standards:

  1. Adequate traffic and pedestrian circulation and access ways shall be required to
  be provided or dedicated and improved as necessary to avoid congestion and to
  prevent adverse effects on neighboring property.
  2. All buildings or structures shall be so arranged as to permit convenient access for
  the City’s emergency and service equipment. Fire hydrants, standpipes and other
  fire protection devices may be required to be installed and maintained at the
  applicant’s expense.
  3. The building and landscaping shall have scale and proportions which relate to its
  size, surroundings and use.
  4. Building elevations shall be designed to be compatible with the characteristics of
  the surrounding areas.
  5. Landscaping, exterior lighting, walls, fences and screen planting shall be
  provided, maintained, and designed to be compatible with the characteristics of
  the surrounding areas.

DISCUSSION
The subject site is currently developed with a commercial building that was built in 1962.
The applicant proposes to conduct interior and exterior improvements to create an office
space for a single tenant. The 4,411 square-foot office space will include individual
offices, an open work area, conference rooms and employee lunch area.

Site Design
The existing commercial building is located on an approximately 18,000 square-foot lot
on Kelso Street. The primary entrance to the office building is along Kelso Street. There
are two additional doors at the rear of the building that open to the rear parking lot.
Parking to the subject site is accessed from a driveway on Kelso Street adjacent to the
subject site.

Architectural Design
The front façade of the existing building currently features two glass entry doors flanked
by two floor to ceiling windows with transparent glass. The building frontage is finished
with a mauve medium stucco finish. A metal awning extends along the building frontage
along with ground level planters. The north facing façade currently has a mural that will
be removed and no windows. The rear of the building contains a window, two doors and
an awning.

The applicant proposes to modify the building exterior by updating it in a modern
architectural style. The building will be painted a charcoal color with a smooth stucco

finish. The existing entry doors will be replaced with two transparent glass entry doors
with a black frame. The applicant also proposes to enhance the building exterior by
reconfiguring and replacing the existing floor to ceiling windows that flank the entry doors
with two six-foot wide windows on both sides of the entry doors. The front façade will be
accented by symmetrically placed, walnut colored wood siding on either side of the
building frontage. The existing awning will be replaced with a flat metal black awning.
Four-foot high planters will be installed with a smooth black stucco finish for the width of
the windows along the building frontage.

The north side of the building will be improved with the installation of three windows and
finished with a smooth charcoal stucco to match the front.

In the rear of the building, the applicant proposes to add a 978 square-foot patio to serve
as an outdoor break area for employees. The exterior rear exit doors will be replaced by
an accordion style glass door with a black frame that opens to the patio. An exit door will
be provided at the rear of the building as well.

Staff has determined that given the location of the site and the proposed use, the Transit
Oriented Development Plan Office Frontage Design Guidelines standards are the
appropriate design guidelines to apply. The exterior improvements comply with the Office
Frontage Design Guidelines as well as the Historic Downtown Design Guidelines of the
Downtown Transit Oriented Development Plan by providing the following features:
   A major pedestrian entry point with a glass façade and pattern of windows.
   Transparent windows.
   Awnings along building frontage.
   Wood accent on frontage to break up blank walls

Design Review Standards
Staff has determined that Design Review Standards have been met as follows:
  1. Adequate traffic and pedestrian circulation and access ways shall be required to
  be provided or dedicated and improved as necessary to avoid congestion and to
  prevent adverse effects on neighboring property. The applicant is seeking approval
  to make exterior improvements to an existing building. Vehicular and pedestrian
  access will be maintained along Kelso Street, or the adjacent driveway and parking
  lot, thereby allowing circulation needs to be met.

  2. All buildings or structures shall be so arranged as to permit convenient access for
  the City’s emergency and service equipment. Fire hydrants, standpipes and other
  fire protection devices may be required to be installed and maintained at the
  applicant’s expense. The site can be directly accessed via Kelso Street or via a
  parking lot directly adjacent to the site. Existing emergency access to the site will
  not be impacted by the exterior modifications.

  3. The building and landscaping shall have scale and proportions which relate to its
  size, surroundings and use. The applicant is proposing to operate an office use
  completely within the building’s interior, with no change to the building footprint or
  building envelope. Thus, the massing of the original building architecture will be

  retained. The proposed building updates will provide landscape planters along the
  front façade similar to surrounding developments. Properties along Kelso are
  developed with primarily one-story buildings that have similar building frontages,
  consisting of awnings, glass entry doors and side accent windows. The proposed
  exterior modifications are consistent with properties of similar size along this
  section of Kelso Street.

  4. Building elevations shall be designed to be compatible with the characteristics of
  the surrounding areas. The scale and architectural character of the building are
  existing and preserve the building sections of Kelso Street. The proposed exterior
  improvements are compatible with the overall design guidelines of the Downtown
  Transit Oriented Districts Development Plan in that it consists of a major pedestrian
  entry point with a glass façade. The architectural scale and building design is
  compatible with surrounding developments. Additionally, the proposed exterior
  improvements contribute an updated enhancement to the building elevations and
  surrounding area.

  5. Landscaping, exterior lighting, walls, fences and screen planting shall be provided,
  maintained, and designed to be compatible with the characteristics of the
  surrounding areas. The landscaping is compatible with surrounding properties
  because properties along Kelso contain ground level and above ground planters.
  No additional lighting is proposed at this time and security fencing is proposed in
  compliance with IMC guidelines.

Signs
The applicant will be required to comply with all IMC sign criteria and permitting
processes.

Security
Currently there are no exterior security cameras on the building. The applicant is
proposing two exterior cameras on the north and south portion of the building frontage
adjacent to the wood siding on Kelso Street. A condition has been added to the Resolution
requiring a minimum of three security cameras be provided on site.

Site Plan Review
If the Planning Commission approves the request, the applicant will be required to
complete the Site Plan Review process. The proposed plans are required to comply with
all applicable provisions of the Zoning Code and receive approval from the Planning
Division, the Public Works Department, and any other applicable City departments.

Area Compatibility
The site is developed in accordance with zoning and development standards for building
height and setbacks for existing commercially-zoned properties. Surrounding land uses
along Kelso Street are developed with commercial uses.

REQUEST
The applicant, Thomas Safran & Associates, is requesting approval to amend exterior
architectural treatments and finishes for the previously approved Design Review for a
mixed- use development that is currently under construction and located at 205 North
Market Street in Downtown Inglewood.

BACKGROUND
In July 2016, the City Council approved a Disposition and Development Agreement with
Thomas Safran & Associates (TSA) to develop the subject property which was city owned
at the time.

On May 3, 2017, the Planning Commission approved Design Review No. 2017-001 (DR-
2017-001) for a mixed-use development consisting of housing units, retail and restaurant
spaces with associated parking spaces.

In March 2019, staff approved the associated Site Plan Review (PR-2017-015) and in
October 2019 the applicant pulled permits and started construction at the vacant site.

In October 2020, the applicant requested City consideration of revised architectural
treatments.

Chapter 12, Article 10.2 and 14 of the Inglewood Municipal Code (IMC) states that in the
MU-1 zone, all exterior improvements (e.g., façade renovation, extension of parapets,
articulation of building walls and entrances, new doors and windows, etc.), extension of
building footprints, and new construction of buildings shall require Design Review
approval.

Design Review is governed by the following Inglewood Municipal Code standards:

  1. Adequate traffic and pedestrian circulation and access ways shall be required to
  be provided or dedicated and improved as necessary to avoid congestion and to
  prevent adverse effects on neighboring property.
  2. All buildings or structures shall be so arranged as to permit convenient access for
  the City’s emergency and service equipment. Fire hydrants, standpipes and other
  fire protection devices may be required to be installed and maintained at the
  applicant’s expense.
  3. The building and landscaping shall have scale and proportions which relate to its
  size, surroundings and use.
  4. Building elevations shall be designed to be compatible with the characteristics of
  the surrounding areas.
  5. Landscaping, exterior lighting, walls, fences and screen planting shall be
  provided, maintained, and designed to be compatible with the characteristics of
  the surrounding areas.

DISCUSSION

The building under construction will be approximately 337,000 square feet and will include
ground floor commercial space with five (5) stories of residential units above. The
residential component will consist of 243 units. The ground floor commercial space will
include restaurant and retail spaces along with a Target store. Parking for the uses on the
property will be located in the core of the structure on floors 1 thru 6. The first level of
parking will be for the ground floor retail uses. Floors 2 thru 6 of the parking will be for
the residents and their guests.

Site Design
Under the revised design, no changes are proposed to the Site Design previously
approved. The 2.77 acre site, currently under construction, is bounded by Florence
Boulevard to the north, Market Street to the east, Regent Street to the south, and La Brea
Boulevard to the west. The Crenshaw/LAX Light Rail Line is currently under construction
to the north of the site along Florence.

Vehicular access to the retail parking is provided via a two-way driveway along Florence
Avenue and a two way driveway on Regent Street. Vehicular access to the residential
parking is provided via a two way driveway along Regent Street. The loading space is
located on the public right-of-way on La Brea Avenue.

Pedestrians will access the ground floor retail and shops from La Brea Avenue, Florence
Avenue, Regent Street and Market Street. Residents and their guests will access the
upper level apartment units from Regent Street. The Target store will be accessed from
the interior of the parking garage on the ground level and La Brea Avenue.

The development includes public plazas with decorative paving, planters and trees that
are adjacent to the tenant spaces at the corners of Market Street and Florence Boulevard
as well as at the corner of Market Street and Regent Street. Additionally, raised planters
are to be installed along the building perimeter on Florence Boulevard and La Brea
Avenue. Onsite trees are located to complement open space areas along Market Street.

Architectural Design
The Downtown Inglewood Transit Oriented Development Plan and Design Guidelines
require pedestrian oriented façade treatments and design compatibility with the Historic
Downtown Design Guidelines (Design Guidelines).

The previously approved design of the mixed-use building was traditional contemporary
and utilized red brick and light earth tone colors. The materials consisted of red brick
veneer, fine and smooth Santa Barbara stucco, traditional horizontal foam trim along the
roofline, horizontal wrought iron balcony enclosures, anodized aluminum storefront
windows along the ground floor, and vinyl windows for the residential units.

   Architectural cornice trims removed
   Color palette changed to darker earth tones, white, and blue
   Balcony railings changed from horizontal bars to vertical

Below is more detail on the changes to materials specific to each elevation:

West Elevation:
  Original Design Features: The approved design included red brick veneer on the
  first floor and corner towers and remaining wall surfaces to be finished with fine
  sand stucco. A metal rooftop canopy was to be attached to the corner tower facing
  La Brea Avenue and Florence Avenue.

  Revised Design: The red brick veneer is removed from this façade of the building
  and replaced with varying types of stucco in darker earth tones. Blue glazed brick
  veneer would be added to a portion of building no. 3 façade. The metal rooftop
  canopy is also proposed to be removed from the corner tower.

North Elevation:
  Original Design Features: The approved design included red brick veneer on
  most of the first floor and the corner towers.

  Revised Design: The red brick veneer is removed from this façade of the building
  and replaced with white and earth toned stucco. Additionally, white brick veneer
  is proposed at the corner of Market Street x Florence Avenue.

MINUTES
  INGLEWOOD SPECIAL PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  WEDNESDAY, JANUARY 20, 2021

(1) PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE:

The City of Inglewood Planning Commission held its Special Planning
Commission meeting on Wednesday, January 20, 2021 in the Council
Chambers on the ninth floor, in City Hall. Following the Pledge of
Allegiance by Commissioner Rice, the meeting was called to order
at 7:01 p.m.

(2) ROLL CALL:

Present:  Commissioner Patricia Patrick
  Commissioner David Rice
  Commissioner Cheryl Shaw-Williams
  Chairman Larry Springs
Excused
Absence:  Commissioner Aide Trejo

Staff:  Mindy Wilcox, AICP, Planning Manager
  Eddy Ikemefuna, Senior Planner
  Jeff Lewis, Assistant City Attorney
  Bernard McCrumby, Planner
  Arturo Salazar, Planner
  Christopher E. Jackson, Sr., Director of E.C.D.
  Evangeline Lane, Secretary
  Via Community Phone Call Coverage:
  AT&T Conference Call Operator Rep.

(3) STAFF COMMUNICATIONS:

Ms. Wilcox stated that Commissioner Trejo advises she will not be
present this evening.

(4) PUBLIC COMMENTS:

None.

The AT&T Operator opened the lines of communication to the public
in order for anyone on the line to speak and give public comments
at this time. There were No Callers on the line.

(5) NON-PUBLIC HEARING:

5A: DESIGN REVIEW NO. 2020-005 (DR-2020-005), 330 EAST KELSO
STREET.
A non-public hearing to consider an application by Sararee
Jirattikanchote, representing Buffalo Wild Wings, for Design
Review No. 2020-005 (DR-2020-005) to allow exterior improvements
to an existing commercial building on an approximately 18,000
square-foot, MU-1(TOD Mixed-Use 1) zoned property at 330 East Kelso
Street.

Mr. Bernard McCrumby, Planner made the staff presentation. He
stated that the applicant is representing TJT Holdings, who is the
property owner and the tenant is who will be speaking before the
Planning Commission this evening.

Chairman Springs opened  with  questions  from  the  Planning
Commission for staff.

Commissioner Patrick one question of staff -
 There appears to be another building next to the 330 Kelso
  Street building, even though it has a different address, will
  this only effect the 330 Kelso Street building and no other
  property in the area?
   Mr. McCrumby answered the question.

Commissioner Rice asked various questions of staff –
 Will there be additional cameras around the building for
  security sake?
 Will there be added Lighting to the exterior of the building to
  make sure there will be no dark areas around the building for
  safety in the evenings?
 With the giant four foot planters that the applicant is going
  to install, where will the water go on the property, who will
  take care of this?
 In the rear of the building, there is a very nice area in the
  patio area, is there a code requirement for the applicant to
  have the BBQ setup on site, will the applicant need a permit in
  order to utilize the BBQ on site?
  - All questions were answered by Mr. McCrumby.

Commissioner Shaw-Williams made a statement to staff -
 Just wanted to insure that the applicant will have or place
  proper lighting throughout the entire complex and property, for
  both pedestrian areas, outside and inside parking areas, as well
  as for the exterior of the buildings.
 To insure no graffiti on the buildings, and Security for the
  safety of the residents.

Chairman  Springs  gave  final  comments  to  staff  regarding  the
project.

Chairman Springs asked the planning commission if there were any
final questions for staff, there were none. He called for the
applicant to come forward and address the planning commission.

Mr. Edward Barnette came forward to speak about the project to the
planning commission.

Chairman Springs asked the  planning  commission  if  they  had
questions for the applicant.

Several of the Planning Commissioners asked a few more questions
of Mr. Barnette.

Commissioner Patrick asked the applicant –
 With the buildings so close together, will the parking in the
  rear be for the 330 Kelso Street employees or will it be shared
  amongst all of the 330 employees?
   Mr. Barnette answered the Commissioner’s question.

Chairman Springs asked if there was a motion on the floor.

MOTION:

The motion was made by Commissioner Rice to affirm the categorical
exemption EA-CE-2020-101, and adopt the attached resolution
approving DR-2020-005 subject to eight (8) existing conditions
with two (2) additional conditions – 1). Enhancing exterior
lighting especially in the front of the building, 2). Adding six
(6) minimum Security Cameras with two on each side of the building,
pointing in cross directions for optimal coverage and was seconded
by Commissioner Patrick, that Resolution No. 1890.
  2

Ms. Wilcox asked for clarification of the number of security
cameras, is it six (6) total or a minimum of six (6).

Commissioner Rice stated it is six (6) minimum.
